survivors.title: kindle_post OCF re-zip stamps every non-mimetype member with wall-clock time → Kindle catalog assets are NOT byte-reproducible
survivors.evidence: Both re-zip sites pass a bare string filename (not a ZipInfo) to writestr: `zout.writestr(name, data[name])` (lines 201 and 662). Python's zipfile, when given a str arcname rather than a ZipInfo, constructs `ZipInfo(filename=name, date_time=time.localtime(time.time())[:6])` — i.e. it stamps the member's central-directory date_time with the CURRENT WALL-CLOCK time. So `make_kindle_safe` (the M4 Send-to-Kindle catalog post-process) and `apply_kindle_m4b` produce a different central directory on every run, even from byte-identical input. No `date_time` is pinned anywhere in the module (grep for `date_time`/`1980`/`_ZIP_EPOCH` returns only `_DOC_SUFFIXES`). This directly contradicts the module docstring: `"-> OCF re-zip (mimetype first + stored)"` described as a "deterministic post-process" (lines 1, 26, 29-32). The sibling packagers DO pin it: build_epub.build sets `zi.date_time = (1980,1,1,0,0,0)` for every entry (build_epub.py:149/156) and swap_epub_cover.swap_cover sets `zi.date_time = _ZIP_EPOCH` (swap_epub_cover.py:33/64). The dedicated guard tests/test_epub_zip_determinism.py asserts `zi.date_time == ZIP_EPOCH` for every entry of build_epub output and documents this exact bug class — but kindle_post was written without applying the same fix, and tests/test_kindle_post.py only checks mimetype-first/stored + content transforms (lines 169-190), never two-build byte equality nor date_time, so the regression escapes. The flagship byte-stability gate (tests/test_byte_stability_gate.py) builds only everywhere-base editions (`_EDITIONS = [ethiopian-tewahedo, catholic-study, evangelical-reformed]`) and never invokes the kindle post-process, so it cannot catch this either. The mimetype member alone is safe (it is written via an explicit `ZipInfo("mimetype")`, whose constructor default date_time is the 1980 epoch). Impact: the shipped Kindle column assets (build_format_matrix.py `_apply_kindle_post` → make_kindle_safe, run LAST on the bytes) and their SHA256SUMS are not reproducible across the required v1.0.0 re-cut (SESSION_STATE: "release assets ... re-cut at tag"), violating the project's core byte-stability invariant for that format.
survivors.fix: Pin every member's date_time (and, to fully match the sibling packagers, external_attr) at both re-zip sites. Define `_ZIP_EPOCH = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)` at module scope and replace the bare-string writestr in the loops with an explicit ZipInfo, mirroring swap_epub_cover.swap_cover: for each non-mimetype `name`, build `zi = zipfile.ZipInfo(name); zi.date_time = _ZIP_EPOCH; zi.external_attr = 0o644 << 16; zi.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED; zout.writestr(zi, data[name], compresslevel=9)`. Also set `date_time`/`external_attr` on the explicit mimetype ZipInfo for parity (lines 197 and 658). Apply identically in both make_kindle_safe (195-201) and apply_kindle_m4b (657-662). Then extend tests/test_kindle_post.py with a determinism case (two make_kindle_safe runs of the same input → identical bytes, and every infolist().date_time == _ZIP_EPOCH), matching test_epub_zip_determinism.py, so this class can never regress again.

survivors.title: Kindle post-process re-zip is non-reproducible (drops the M14 date_time / external_attr pin) — 2 sibling sites
survivors.evidence:

```
with zipfile.ZipFile(dst_epub, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zout:
    zout.writestr(zipfile.ZipInfo("mimetype"), data["mimetype"], compress_type=zipfile.ZIP_STORED)
```

result.fixesPlanMarkdown:
## Executive summary

This round-10 deep audit produced **11 deduped findings → 8 verified survivors (3 refuted)**; of the survivors, **6 are bug/correctness/debt findings and 2 are optimization recommendations**, with severity distribution **{high: 1, medium: 1, low: 5, info: 1}**. The most serious is the **HIGH** cache-discipline gate failure: a new `@lru_cache` on `_estimate_kepub_aside_bytes` is neither whitelisted nor cleared, turning three `test_audit_caches` tests red — a red commit gate, not a content defect. The one **MEDIUM** is a real byte-stability hole: `kindle_post.py` re-zips with bare-string `writestr`, stamping wall-clock `date_time` into every member so the M4 Kindle catalog assets are not reproducible across the v1.0.0 re-cut. The remaining five LOWs are stale config/test drift and dev-only Kobo tooling decay, none of which touch the shipped Ethiopian artifact's content. Overall codebase health is strong: no silent data loss, no security exposure, the 9 KJV editions remain byte-stable, and every finding is additive or test/dev-only — the engine and the marathon core are untouched.

## Phased fixes

### Phase 1 — Green the commit gates (additive metadata + test-only; zero output change)

- [ ] **[HIGH] Whitelist the new pure-function cache** — `scripts/build_edition.py:3301-3302` (`@lru_cache(maxsize=8192)` on `_estimate_kepub_aside_bytes`). **Fix:** add one whitelist line to `scripts/.cache_audit_whitelist.py` under the existing "Pure-function compiled-regex caches" section: `_._estimate_kepub_aside_bytes  # scripts/build_edition.py — pure post-kepubify byte estimate keyed only on html_text (Opt#5); depends solely on the arg + immutable constants _KEPUB_SENTENCE_RE / _KEPUB_SPAN_OVERHEAD; no write path can invalidate it`. Do **NOT** add a `cache_clear()` call (it would be dead code for a pure function). **Guard:** the existing `tests/test_audit_caches.py` family is the guard — it goes green automatically (no_clear_path 1→0; the 3 failing tests pass). Confirm `scripts/audit_caches.py` returns `ok=True`. **Build path:** audit-only metadata; 9 KJV editions stay byte-identical → no byte-stability re-cut needed.

- [ ] **[LOW] Drop the stale `theme: "modern"` pin** — `content/editions.yaml:186` (catholic-study; the only edition pinning a theme SKU). **Fix:** remove line 186; `edition.get("theme", "classic")` then defaults to classic, matching the module docstring. Write via the atomic-write/save path (editions.yaml is conftest-protected). Do **NOT** weaken `test_themes.py` — the docstring makes the test the source of truth. **Guard:** existing `tests/test_themes.py::test_editions_do_not_pin_theme_skus` re-greens. **Build path:** KJV editions carry no theme pin and are unaffected; catholic-study is canon-filtered — verify a catholic-study build is unchanged (theme is build-time-selected, so default `classic` ≠ the stale `modern` only matters if a build previously consumed it; confirm no output diff).

- [ ] **[LOW] Repoint the now-stale dedup-default test** — `tests/test_note_rehaul.py:240-242` (asserts catholic-study surfaces `note_attribution_dedup is False`, but that edition now intentionally pins `true`; all four canon editions pin `true` by design). **Fix:** test-only. Do **NOT** touch `content/editions.yaml`. Repoint the assertion at the **code default** rather than a specific shipped edition: feed a stub edition dict lacking the key through the same `api_customize_data` passthrough and assert the emitted row is `False`, plus assert `isinstance(e["note_attribution_dedup"], bool)` for every shipped edition. **Guard:** the rewritten test is the guard (cannot re-stale when rollout pins change). **Build path:** none (test-only).

### Phase 2 — Byte-stability: pin the Kindle re-zip (build-path; byte-stability proof obligation)

- [ ] **[MEDIUM / OPT-dup] Pin `date_time` + `external_attr` in both Kindle re-zip sites** — `scripts/core/kindle_post.py:195-201` (`make_kindle_safe`) and `:657-662` (`apply_kindle_m4b`). Both pass a bare string to `writestr`, so zipfile stamps `date_time = time.localtime(time.time())[:6]` → non-reproducible central directory, contradicting the module's "deterministic post-process" docstring and diverging from `build_epub.py:149/156` and `swap_epub_cover.py:33/64` which pin the M14 epoch. **Fix:** add module-scope `_ZIP_EPOCH = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)`; at **both** sites write the mimetype via an explicit `ZipInfo` and loop members with a per-member `ZipInfo` whose `date_time = _ZIP_EPOCH`, `external_attr = 0o644 << 16`, `compress_type = ZIP_DEFLATED` (add `compresslevel=9` to match the sibling packagers; optional but recommended for consistency). The `date_time` + `external_attr` pin is the load-bearing part. Apply **identically at both sites** (whole-class sweep: these are the only two defective re-zip sites; `build_epub.py`/`swap_epub_cover.py` already pin correctly; `build_standalone.py` is off-limits). **Guard:** add a determinism case to `tests/test_kindle_post.py` mirroring `tests/test_epub_zip_determinism.py` — run `make_kindle_safe` (and `apply_kindle_m4b`) twice on the same synthetic input, assert byte-identical output, and assert every `infolist().date_time == _ZIP_EPOCH`. **Build path:** YES — this is the Kindle column's final transform. **Byte-stability proof obligation:** the 9 KJV editions don't run the Kindle post-process and stay byte-identical (prove via regen + `git diff`); the Kindle artifact's bytes/SHA256 *change once* (the fix) then become stable across the v1.0.0 re-cut — that is the intended outcome.

### Phase 3 — Dev-only Kobo tooling decay (no engine/output/byte impact)

- [ ] **[LOW] Finish the round-5 sync in the tap-calibration tool** — `dev/kobo_tap_calibration.py:6-17, 32, 79`. The turn-119 fix updated `BRACKET_LO=4_498`/`BRACKET_HI=5_500` but left the docstring (round-4 `3,313 < T <= 7,748`), `DEFAULT_TARGETS = (3_500…7_500)`, and the probe targets stale → 4 of 5 default targets fall outside the strict `(4_498, 5_500)` pool, collapsing every probe onto one band. This tool is the live round-9 oracle (`scripts/reader_sim.py:233` runs it verbatim; `EREADERS.md §Kobo round-9`). **Fix:** (1) update the docstring/example to round-5 numbers; (2) set `DEFAULT_TARGETS` inside the band, e.g. `(4_600, 4_800, 5_000, 5_200, 5_400)`; (3) **load-bearing:** make `pick_probes` degrade gracefully — fall back to the nearest-overall aside (not pool-restricted) per target when the in-band pool is sparse/empty, so distinct rows are returned instead of silently dropped. **Guard:** add a unit test pinning `DEFAULT_TARGETS ⊂ (BRACKET_LO, BRACKET_HI)` and that `pick_probes` returns distinct asides for in-band targets and falls back on an empty band. **Build path:** none (dev-only tool).

- [ ] **[LOW] Add a non-failing oversize-piece WARN to the kepub verifier** — `dev/verify_kr2_build.py:500-535, 722-726`. Gate 1 computes per-piece sizes but only prints them; no ceiling is asserted, and the shipped round-9 ethiopian kepub reached an 882 KB piece — past the 881 KB size `EREADERS.md:93-94` records as having broken Kobo rendering. **Fix:** after the size loop, compute byte sizes (`len(zf.read(n))`, not codepoints) and `print` a `WARN (1-size)` line for any piece over a ~500 KB comfort threshold. **Keep it a WARN** — never `fails.append` — so the already-accepted round-9/13 device-PASS artifact (and the byte-stable KJV editions) are not regressed into a new FAIL. Do **NOT** add a builder sub-cut (the glossary chunker already cuts at study-glossary-entry boundaries, `build_edition.py:4971-4978`); lowering `FILE_SPLIT_TARGET_DEFAULT` is the existing round-9 P2 deferral, editorial/QA-gated, only if a real device paging failure is ever evidenced (none on record). **Build path:** none (verifier-only WARN).

### Recurring-invariant note (lint vs pytest)
The cache-discipline invariant (Phase 1 HIGH) recurs on **every** new `@lru_cache`, so the commit-time check is the right home — `scripts/audit_caches.py` already runs as that lint and `tests/test_audit_caches.py` mirrors it; keep the whitelist the single source of truth rather than relying on a pytest-only guard. The byte-stability invariant (Phase 2) should remain enforced by the determinism unit test plus the regen-and-`git diff` obligation; a commit-time `lint_rules` check that flags any `writestr(<str>, …)` in OCF packagers (i.e. requiring a pinned `ZipInfo`) would prevent the whole class from recurring — recommended as a follow-up backstop.

## Optimization decisions

| Area | Verdict | Recommendation |
|------|---------|----------------|
| Kindle post-process re-zip (`kindle_post.py:195-201, 657-662`) | **change** | Pin `date_time = (1980,1,1,0,0,0)` + `external_attr = 0o644 << 16` per member at both sites; add `compresslevel=9` for sibling-packager consistency. Restores M14 reproducibility; this is the same defect as the Phase-2 MEDIUM (one fix satisfies both). No paid API; KJV editions stay byte-stable. |
| Build `inject → filter → zip` pipeline (`build_edition.py:7408-7847, 7934-7939`) | **confirmed-optimal** | No change. Per-edition copytree + in-memory consolidated passes (Round-9 Opt#2) + content-addressable `build_cache` + `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=≤5)` already exhausts safe speedups. compresslevel 9→6 DECLINED on merits; no shared post-filter prefix exists (editions diverge at the first filter pass); more workers OOM the 16 GB box. Irreducible floor = genuinely-parallel per-edition zip. |
| Marathon core (`build_standalone.py`, `core/manuscript_*.py`, `core/po_vision_store.py`, `content/manuscript/**`, patrologia, GAPS) | **off-limits** | Not evaluated and not to be edited — read-only context per the off-limits directive. |

**Constraints on all optimization work:** no paid/external API (Voyage integration dropped; key-rotation security only); every change must preserve byte-identical output for the 9 KJV editions, proven by regen + `git diff`.

## Constraints carried

- **Never touch the marathon core**: `scripts/build_standalone.py`, `scripts/core/manuscript_*.py`, `scripts/core/po_vision_store.py`, `content/manuscript/**`, `content/translations/sources/patrologia/**`, `GAPS/`.
- **9 KJV editions must build byte-stable**; any schema change is **additive** (byte-identical when unset). Phase-2 is the only build-path change and carries the regen-and-`git diff` proof obligation (KJV unaffected; Kindle artifact changes once then stabilizes).
- **Atomic writes**: all config/store writes go through `notes_io.atomic_write` / `ensure_backup`; `editions.yaml` is conftest-protected → edit via the atomic-write/save path.
- **No paid/external API**; single-user LOCAL desktop app — CSRF / rate-limiting / public-server hardening / multi-tenant auth remain out of scope.
- **Save cadence (RULES §4, 2026-06-08)**: each fix lands as a **LOCAL COMMIT**; the full **5-leg sync** (`save-all.ps1`: local + GitLab + GitHub + E: + F:) happens **only at a milestone** or on an explicit user save/push command.
- **This audit is FINDINGS-ONLY**: this is the plan. **STOP before applying any fix** (user marching order 2026-06-08) — no edits, no commits until directed.
